questions.stem: The parliament of Israel is known as:
questions.explanation: Each country's parliament has a distinctive name — commonly tested: KNESSET (Israel, unicameral 120 members), DIET (Japan — National Diet; Germany called its lower house the 'Bundestag' but Imperial Germany used 'Reichstag' = 'Diet of the Empire'), MAJLIS (Iran and several Arab states), SEJM (Poland, lower house), DUMA (Russia lower house, State Duma; upper = Federation Council), BUNDESTAG (Germany lower house, Bundesrat upper), CORTES (Spain), SHURA (Saudi Arabia consultative), RIKSDAG (Sweden), STORTING (Norway), FOLKETING (Denmark), ALTHING (Iceland — world's oldest, est. 930 AD), NATIONAL PEOPLE'S CONGRESS (China), CONGRESS (USA — Senate + House of Rep), PARLIAMENT (UK, India).

questions.stem: The currency of which country is the 'Ngultrum'?
questions.explanation: NGULTRUM (BTN) is Bhutan's currency, pegged at par with the Indian Rupee. Indian Rupee is also accepted freely in Bhutan. Neighbours: Nepal = Nepalese Rupee (NPR, also pegged to INR at ~1.6 NPR = 1 INR); Sri Lanka = Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR); Myanmar = Kyat (MMK); Bangladesh = Taka (BDT); Pakistan = Pakistani Rupee (PKR); Maldives = Rufiyaa (MVR); Afghanistan = Afghani (AFN). Often-confused currencies: Renminbi/Yuan (China), Yen (Japan), Won (Korea), Riyal (Saudi/Qatar/Oman/Yemen), Dinar (Kuwait/Bahrain/Jordan/Algeria/Iraq/Libya/Tunisia), Dirham (UAE/Morocco).

questions.stem: South Africa has three capitals. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: South Africa uniquely has THREE constitutional capitals representing different branches: PRETORIA = Executive (seat of President, Cabinet); CAPE TOWN = Legislative (Parliament sits here); BLOEMFONTEIN = Judicial (Supreme Court of Appeal). Johannesburg — though the largest, richest city and financial hub — is NOT a capital. Other multi-capital countries: Netherlands (Amsterdam constitutional + The Hague seat of govt), Sri Lanka (Colombo commercial + Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte legislative), Bolivia (Sucre constitutional + La Paz seat of govt), Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur official + Putrajaya administrative), Chile (Santiago executive + Valparaiso legislative).

questions.stem: Which landlocked country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.explanation: LESOTHO is one of only 3 countries in the world ENTIRELY ENCLAVED by another single country (completely surrounded by South Africa). The other two enclaved states: VATICAN CITY (inside Rome, Italy) and SAN MARINO (inside Italy). Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is almost surrounded by SA but has a short border with Mozambique. Capital of Lesotho: Maseru. Currency: Loti (LSL, pegged to ZAR). Landlocked African countries to know: Burkina Faso, Burundi, CAR, Chad, Ethiopia, Malawi, Mali, Niger, Rwanda, South Sudan, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Largest landlocked country globally: Kazakhstan.

questions.stem: The currency 'Dong' belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: DONG (VND) is Vietnam's currency. SE Asian currencies: Thailand = Baht; Cambodia = Riel; Laos = Kip; Indonesia = Rupiah; Philippines = Peso; Malaysia = Ringgit; Singapore = Singapore Dollar; Brunei = Brunei Dollar; Myanmar = Kyat; East Timor = US Dollar; S Korea = Won; N Korea = Won (different); Japan = Yen; China = Yuan/Renminbi; Taiwan = New Taiwan Dollar; Mongolia = Tugrik. Vietnamese capital: Hanoi (not Ho Chi Minh City — that's the largest city).

questions.stem: The 'Storting' is the parliament of which country?
questions.explanation: STORTING = Norway. Nordic parliaments: NORWAY = Storting (unicameral, 169 members, Oslo); SWEDEN = Riksdag (unicameral, 349 members, Stockholm); DENMARK = Folketing (unicameral, 179 members, Copenhagen); FINLAND = Eduskunta (unicameral, 200 members, Helsinki); ICELAND = Althing/Alþingi (unicameral, 63 members, Reykjavik) — world's OLDEST surviving parliament, founded 930 AD by the Vikings at Þingvellir. Memorise at least 15 world parliament names for exam-level preparation.

questions.stem: Abuja is the capital of which African country, known for having replaced Lagos as capital in 1991?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shifted its capital from Lagos (coastal, overcrowded, southern) to Abuja (central, purpose-built) on 12 December 1991 for geographical centrality and ethno-religious neutrality. Similar capital shifts: Brazil (Rio → Brasilia 1960), Pakistan (Karachi → Islamabad 1960-67), Kazakhstan (Almaty → Astana/Nur-Sultan/Astana 1997 — renamed back), Myanmar (Yangon → Naypyidaw 2006), Egypt (Cairo → New Administrative Capital, under construction), Indonesia (Jakarta → Nusantara, planned 2024+). African capitals worth knowing: Addis Ababa (Ethiopia, HQ of African Union), Accra (Ghana), Nairobi (Kenya), Kampala (Uganda), Dar es Salaam (Tanzania's commercial capital; Dodoma is official), Kigali (Rwanda), Luanda (Angola).

questions.stem: The currency of which country is 'Shekel'?
questions.explanation: Israeli NEW SHEKEL (ILS) — Israel. Middle East currencies: Lebanon = Lebanese Pound/Lira; Jordan = Jordanian Dinar (JOD — one of the strongest currencies); Iran = Iranian Rial; Iraq = Iraqi Dinar; Saudi = Riyal; UAE = Dirham; Bahrain = Dinar; Kuwait = Kuwaiti Dinar (strongest currency globally by exchange rate against USD); Qatar = Riyal; Oman = Omani Rial (3rd strongest); Yemen = Yemeni Rial; Syria = Syrian Pound; Turkey = Turkish Lira. The name 'Shekel' (שקל) dates back to ancient biblical times; the NEW shekel replaced the old shekel (1985) at 1000:1.

questions.stem: Which country was formerly known as 'Siam', changed its name in 1939?
questions.explanation: Siam was renamed THAILAND (= 'land of the free') in 1939 under PM Plaek Phibunsongkhram. Notable country renamings: Burma → Myanmar (1989, military junta); Ceylon → Sri Lanka (1972); Kampuchea ↔ Cambodia (1975 Khmer Rouge renamed to Kampuchea; reverted 1989); Persia → Iran (1935); Abyssinia → Ethiopia (1940s); Rhodesia → Zimbabwe (1980 independence); Upper Volta → Burkina Faso (1984); Zaire → Democratic Republic of the Congo (1997); Swaziland → Eswatini (2018); Turkey → Türkiye (official 2022). Cities: Bombay → Mumbai (1995), Madras → Chennai (1996), Calcutta → Kolkata (2001), Bangalore → Bengaluru (2014), Peking → Beijing (1979).
